newsitem.title: USA: Dow claws to record but broader market pauses.
newsitem.headline: Dow claws to record but broader market pauses.

text.p: The Dow industrials scraped out a second consecutive record close on Tuesday after a hesitant session that left the broad market mixed.

The blue chip average gained 11 points to close unofficially at an all-time high 7225. Despite the record, stocks clearly lacked the sizzle that sent a bevy of Wall Street records toppling just a day ago.
"The action today was indicative of the market's split personality," said Charlie Crane, chief market strategist at Key Asset Management.
"The technical condition of the market remains outstanding, and the breadth has been impressive in recent sessions," Crane said. "But then on the other hand, we've come a long way."
Broad indices showed little change on the day, with advancing issues and decliners running in a near-dead heat. Small-cap stocks ended a trace lower, halting a recent spree.
But the tame performance at the index level masked a frenzied day in terms of volume. On the New York Stock Exchange, more than 600 million shares changed hands for only the seventh time in history.

Analysts said the swift recovery in equity prices had likely rekindled interest among momentum investors eager to hop back into an apparently resurgent bull market, but observers cautioned that near-term gains were likely to be limited with stocks again at lofty levels.

"I do feel the bulk of the near-term gains are probably already in the market, and that's looking both technically and rationally," said Joseph Barthel, chief investment strategist at Fahnestock & Co.
Still, Barthel said the rally's momentum, which has lifted several indices to records, may foreshadow more gains.
"We'll probably get a period of consolidation, but rallies don't usually end in a one-time burst like this," he said. "I'm certainly very optimistic."
To be sure, several factors could hold the market in check for the next couple of weeks, most importantly the approaching May 20 meeting of the Federal Reserve's interest rate policy-makers.

Wall Street is more divided on whether that meeting will result in an interest rate increase than they were heading into the Fed's March meeting. Some analysts say that uncertainty may not bode well for stocks.

"Everybody in March knew they were going to raise rates and it still caused a considerable amount of indigestion when they did," Crane said. With the market seemingly less prepared this time around, a May move could prove even more upsetting, he said.
Tech stocks ended broadly lower, amid profit-taking and a weak showing from bellwether chip maker Intel Corp.
Intel slid 4-1/2 to 158 as concerns emerged about a possible flaw in the company's high-end Pentium II and Pentium Pro processers. Several investment firms also downgraded the shares Tuesday.
Internet sevice provider BBN Corp jumped 6-1/4 to 28-7/8 after accepting a $29-per-share acquisition offer from telecommunications company GTE Corp.
GTE fell 2-3/8 to 45 after it said it now expected 1997 earnings-per-share growth to be slightly positive at best, instead of in double digits as it earlier forecast.
BTG Inc tumbled 5-7/16 to 9-13/16. Late Monday, the company reported a fourth-quarter loss and said it had fallen out of compliance on lending covenants, for which it was seeking waivers.
The Nasdaq Composite fell 10.94 points to 1328.30.
The S&P 500 index fell 2.48 points to 827.76.
((-- Wall Street desk, 212-859-1730))
